overview: Angola is a country on the Atlantic coast of southern Africa. Its capital and largest city is Luanda. Angola became independent from Portugal in 1975, and a long civil war followed that ended in 2002. Portuguese is the official language, and Angola is one of Africa's biggest oil producers; Cabinda, a province cut off from the rest of the country by DR Congo, produces much of the oil.

geography.text: Angola has a narrow coastal plain, behind which the land rises sharply to a high central plateau. The north is covered by tropical forest and grassland, while the south-west includes part of the Namib Desert. Many rivers begin in Angola's highlands, including tributaries of the Congo and the Zambezi.

history.text: The Kingdom of Kongo and the Ndongo kingdom ruled parts of the region when the Portuguese arrived in the late 1400s. Angola became a centre of the Atlantic slave trade, and Portugal ruled it for centuries. After a long war of independence, Angola became independent in 1975, but a civil war followed that lasted until 2002.

events.title: Portuguese arrive
events.text: Portuguese sailors reach the mouth of the Congo River.

events.title: Queen Nzinga
events.text: Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba begins decades of resistance to Portugal.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Angola becomes independent and civil war begins.

events.title: Civil war ends
events.text: A ceasefire ends 27 years of war.
